name: Hasadiah
overview: Hasadiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Meshullam. The biblical record mentions him briefly without additional personal details or notable events. His mention situates him within the genealogical context of Judah's lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Hasadiah means 'y-h-v-h is faithful,' reflecting a theologically rich affirmation of God's faithfulness. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:20, highlights the spiritual significance often found in Hebrew names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hasadiah as the son of Meshullam, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hasadiah's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical records of Judah, as preserved in 1 Chronicles 3:20. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or roles, his inclusion affirms the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage through which the Messiah would eventually come. This genealogical mention supports the biblical narrative of God's providential care over His people.
